name: MLGym
intro: MLGym是首个面向机器学习任务的Gym环境，支持大型语言模型代理的评估与开发。它包含13个多样化且开放式的AI研究任务，涵盖计算机视觉、自然语言处理和强化学习等领域，旨在促进对AI研究型Agent的开发与评估。
build_method: 专家任务策展, 可配置Gym沙盒, 脚本化评测
metric: Best Attempt@4、Best Submission@4、性能剖面曲线下面积、任务专用指标
modality: 文本, 图像, 代码, 多模态
build_method_en: Expert task curation, configurable Gym sandboxing, script-based evaluation
intro_en: MLGym is the first Gym environment designed for machine learning tasks, supporting the evaluation and development of large language model agents. It includes 13 diverse and open-ended AI research tasks spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, aiming to advance the development and assessment of AI research agents.

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit completed 2026-07-21 against arXiv:2502.14499v1 (the sole paper revision, submitted 2025-02-20 12:28:23 UTC; PDF SHA-256 c734f3727a85a8cb7c4f118eae946a253e93624f32c170b086d14caf1fe857bc), the last official facebookresearch/MLGym commit before that submission (075634859ec3ab16c56ca87678ec0fe564a27470, committed 2025-02-19T15:28:45-08:00), and public HEAD 9d40c1b5035202018cd7091fb4e83a9c68b377c0 dated 2025-08-10. The pinned registry contains 13 paper tasks: House Price, 3-SAT, CIFAR-10, Fashion MNIST, MS-COCO, FineWeb language modeling, MNLI, Battle of Sexes, Prisoner's Dilemma, Blotto, Breakout, Meta Maze, and Mountain Car Continuous. That is one tabular task, one SAT task, three games, three vision tasks, two NLP tasks, and three RL tasks; the paper prose says four main categories while listing five and treating SAT separately, so the figure reports the registry census. The pinned source has 18 task YAMLs, 7 dataset YAMLs, and 261 trajectory/result pairs: 13 tasks x 5 models x 4 runs plus one FineWeb LM test pair. No Git tag pins this state. Dataset provenance is split between Hugging Face (CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, MNLI) and Drive/local inputs (House Prices, COCO, FineWeb, 3-SAT). House Prices uses a 70/10/20 split with seed 42; COCO train/validation remove human-containing images; FineWeb declares regex train/valid/test files while paper and config token counts differ. The paper/source do not disclose a benchmark-wide split protocol, dataset checksums, curator/reviewer counts, task acceptance rates, comprehensive deduplication, leakage testing, or a uniform QC procedure. All 13 paper task configs mark evaluation_read_only true. Most task timeouts are 1,800 seconds; COCO, FineWeb, and MNLI use 2,400 seconds. Submission contracts comprise four CSV tasks, two model/language-model state tasks, four target.py tasks, and three RL tasks requiring a config plus five checkpoints. The public boundary includes configs, code, evaluators, published tables, trajectories, and score vectors, but large dataset bytes use mutable Drive/Hugging Face references, the image is aigym/mlgym-agent:latest, and dataset hashes are absent. The repository is principally CC-BY-NC 4.0 with mixed subcomponent licenses, so public availability is not a content-pinned redistribution bundle. The paper-period experiment launchers are not directly runnable as published: they pass --config_file although run.py exposes agent_config_path; reference absent configs/agents/better_thought_action_parser_with_insert.yaml and docker/aliases_docker.sh; and 3SAT.sh names absent tasks/3SAT.yaml instead of tasks/3SATTime.yaml. Later HEAD changes those references to --agent_config_path, configs/agents/default.yaml, docker/aliases.sh, and tasks/3SATTime.yaml; these repairs are later drift, not evidence of a runnable paper snapshot. The executable harness still establishes the paper-main SWE-Agent ReAct semantics: a non-root Docker/Podman workspace, read-only local data and evaluator, runtime Hugging Face fetches, core file/search/shell plus validate/submit tools, one command per step, a 1,000-line view, last-five-interaction context, up to 50 steps, task timeouts, and a USD 4 launcher cap. Literature-search and memory tools exist but are outside the paper-main setup. validate evaluates without terminating and appends only a valid metric to info.score. submit and automatic terminal evaluation end the run; an invalid terminal artifact may append no score. Released failure analysis classifies an empty agent score vector as failed, but a non-success termination after a prior valid score as incomplete. Separately, the released ranker uses results.agent[-1] as its last-submission proxy whenever a valid score exists; the figure distinguishes that fallback from the paper's final-submission definition. Best Attempt@4 takes the best valid logged metric across four runs, while the paper's Best Submission@4 takes the best final submission. The paper calls the four runs independently seeded, but released launchers only number run directories 0-3, EnvironmentArguments.seed defaults to 42, and run.py does not vary it. A model with no valid result or no baseline improvement is infeasible and receives epsilon 0.05 handling. Performance-profile ratios respect metric direction, rho(tau) is the fraction of 13 tasks within the log10-ratio threshold, and step-area AUP is reported for both @4 views with raw metrics and cost; confidence intervals are not reported. Public HEAD has 19 task and 8 dataset YAMLs, adds Titanic, changes the 3-SAT/FineWeb evaluation surface, and differs from the pinned snapshot in 1,506 tracked files; these changes remain a drift branch. The bilingual source specs are isomorphic across 20 nodes and 21 edges, and all three Mermaid fallbacks are synchronized from those specs. Nodes inherit the academic-color default font size 11 with no per-node override. Temporary --validate --strict generation exited 0 for both languages and XML validation passed; the CLI reported only its 20 per-node informational label-length advisories, with no warning, error, or fatal item. Draw.io Desktop PNGs measured 1625x845 in both languages; 0.9x previews measured 1463x761. Both scales and languages were visually checked for clipping, text overlap, edge-through-label routing, and branch clarity; no blocking defect remained. Formal publication evidence [site-a11l-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1605×825 (English) and 1605×825 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1603×823 and 1603×823. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
